newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault falls as analysts cut estimates.
newsitem.headline: Renault falls as analysts cut estimates.

text.p: Shares in French carmaker Renault extended their losses on Monday after industry analysts cut their results forecasts for 1997 and 1998 for the group after its profit warning on Friday.
The stock finished down 2.94 percent at 118.90 francs on Monday. It had fallen 5.76 percent on Friday.

Societe Generale cuts its earnings per share (EPS) estimate for the group to a loss of seven francs for 1997 from a loss of 2.9 francs previously and to a loss of 2.5 francs for 1998 from a profit of 2.10 francs previously.

Societe Generale expects an operating loss of 1.1 billion francs for 1997, including a 1.5 billion franc operating loss in Renault's car division. It previously forecast a 400 million operating loss in that branch. For the trucks unit, it expects a one billion franc operating loss for 1997 and it expects a 1.4 billion franc profit for the financial unit.

Cheuvreux de Virieu lowered its EPS forecast to a loss of 2.9 francs for 1997 from a loss of 0.4 franc previously. It estimates Renault's EPS loss for 1996 at 8.3 francs, down from a loss of 4.2 francs previously.
Du Bouzet, BNP's brokerage arm, and CS First Boston also cut their forecasts, market sources said. Du Bouzet confirmed it had lowered its estimates but declined to disclose them.

Consultants Jacques Chahine Finance said several brokers had revised their forecasts on Friday and Monday after Renault's latest profit warning. The consensus estimate had been for a loss of 800 million francs for 1996.

Renault said in its 1996 sales statement on Friday that "In view of the prevailing economic context, and despite the increase in revenues of the automobile division ... the operating loss to be reported by Renault Group for 1996 will be considerably higher than that generally anticipated by the financial markets".

The markets were anticipating an operating loss of between 1.3 and 1.6 billion francs for 1996 broken down into an operating loss of around two billion francs in the car division, an operating loss of 600 million or more francs in the trucks division, and an operating profit at the finance unit.

Several analysts said on Friday that the profit warning had led them to expect an operating loss of between 2.8 and 3.5 billion francs in the car division, resulting in a 1996 net loss estimated at more than two billion francs for the group.
